display_name: Singapore -- a citizen's foreign spouse: Long-Term Visit Pass, permanent residence and citizenship, as ICA publishes them
citation: Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (Singapore), web pages 'Apply for Singapore Citizenship', 'Oath-taking for Minors', 'Apply for Permanent Residence', 'Apply for Long-Term Visit Pass' (and its spouse-of-a-Singapore-citizen page) and 'Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment'

source.note: ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY AS PUBLISHED, NOT LAW. These are ICA's web pages describing who may apply for a Long-Term Visit Pass, permanent residence and citizenship as the spouse of a Singapore citizen, with fees and processing times. ICA can change them at any time without legislation; the pages carry 'Last updated' dates but no effective dates. The policy operates under the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (citizenship by registration, Art 123(2); the oath, Art 126; renunciation, Art 128 -- row constitution-of-the-republic-of-singapore/naive-2026-10) and the Immigration Act 1959 (entry permits, s 10; passes by regulations, s 55(1)(c) -- row immigration-act-1959/naive-2026-10). The Immigration Regulations, which create the long-term visit pass, are not deposited. The statutory tests belong to those rows; this subject records only what ICA says it does.
